display.title: Episode 240: Reb Yosef Mokir Shabbos (Shabbos Mevarchim Elul)
display.summary_short: Before Elul, Uncle Yossi explains the Alter Rebbe's parable of the King in the field, then tells how Yosef, who honored Shabbos, found a fortune inside a fish.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Shabbos Mevarchim Elul, Parshas Re'eh, 5746. Uncle Yossi explains that Elul, the last month of the year, prepares us for the new year, and brings the Alter Rebbe's parable from Likkutei Torah: during Elul, Hashem is like a king who has left his palace and is passing through the fields, where anyone can greet him and he receives everyone with a shining face. After the Hakochainik march, a boy from Yeshiva Ohalei Torah leads the Shema. Story time: Yosef Mokir Shabbos buys the biggest fish every week and shares gefilte fish with the town's poor, while a selfish rich neighbor, warned by a stargazer that his wealth will pass to Yosef, sells everything for one diamond and sews it into his hat. The wind blows the hat into the sea and the diamond is lost. One Friday a fisherman sells Yosef a huge fish for thirteen gold coins, and inside it is the diamond. Whoever spends for Shabbos, Shabbos repays him. Uncle Yossi closes with Elul's lesson: guard our actions, speech and even thoughts, and chase away the yetzer hara with the Twelve Pesukim.
display.lesson: Whatever you spend in honor of Shabbos, Shabbos repays; in Elul, guard your deeds, words and even your thoughts.
